title: Two-Signal Interval Sweeper
prompt:
Implement `active_overlap_intervals(left_events, right_events, horizon) -> list[tuple[int, int]]`. Each event stream contains strictly time-increasing `(timestamp, active)` updates for one signal. Both signals start inactive. An update at time `t` takes effect for the half-open interval beginning at `t`; `horizon` is an integer end time, and every event timestamp must satisfy `0 <= timestamp < horizon`.

Return the maximal half-open intervals `[start, end)` within `[0, horizon)` during which both signals are active. At a timestamp that appears in both streams, apply the entire timestamp batch before deciding the state of the following interval. Therefore simultaneous changes never create a zero-length transient interval.

Timestamps must be integers but not booleans, and `active` must be a boolean. Reject malformed, out-of-order, duplicate-timestamp, or out-of-horizon events with `ValueError`. Do not mutate either input stream. Use only the Python standard library.

example.input: left = [(1, True), (4, False)]; right = [(2, True), (5, False)]; active_overlap_intervals(left, right, 6)
example.reasoning: Both signals are active only after the right update at 2 and before the left update at 4.
